basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Cum ergo occubuisset sol, facta est caligo tenebrosa, et apparuit clibanus fumigans, et'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Cum ergo occubuisset sol, facta est caligo tenebrosa, et apparuit clibanus fumigans, et lampas ignis transiens inter divisiones illas. Haec caligo et clibanus ignis post occasum solis factus, significat jam in fine saeculi per ignem judicandos esse carnales. Sicut enim afflictio civitatis Dei, qualis antea nunquam fuit quae sub Antichristo futura speratur, significatur tenebroso timore Abrahae circa solis occasum, id est, propinquante jam fine saeculi; sic ad solis occasum, id est, ad ipsum jam finem, significatur isto igne dies judicii dirimens carnales per ignem salvandos et in igne damnandos.
